Thanks - Priya

- TDC net sales up 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, including two new hyperscale awards.

# Veridane Fluid Technologies, Inc. — Q3 FY2026 Letter to Shareholders
**DRAFT — pending review by Dana Whitcombe and Mark Ostrander — not for release**
*(Format and voice follow the Q2 FY2026 letter: highlights, segment review, outlook, closing.)*

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

The growth engine at Veridane accelerated in the third quarter. Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC) grew net sales 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, we won two new hyperscale awards, and our data-center cooling backlog reached a record $574.2 million, up 22.0%. Total backlog also set a record at $918.0 million, up 13.0% year over year — the clearest signal of the demand we are capturing as liquid cooling scales across the industry.

The quarter also demanded decisiveness, and we moved quickly. Core commercial HVAC remained soft, and we launched a voluntary recall of certain GV-400 series gas valves — a proactive, customer-first action taken in cooperation with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) under its Fast Track program. We moved just as aggressively on cost: Project Keystone, our simplification and savings program, is on track to deliver $35 million of run-rate savings by the second quarter of fiscal 2027.

## Highlights

- TDC net sales up 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, including two new hyperscale awards.
- Record total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0% year over year; data-center cooling backlog up 22.0% to a record $574.2 million.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million; adjusted EPS of $0.15, reflecting the softer BCV environment.
- GV-400 recall launched proactively under CPSC Fast Track; replacement valves have been shipping since late September and no injuries have been reported.
- Project Keystone on track to deliver $35 million of run-rate savings by Q2 FY2027.
- GAAP results for the quarter, including net income and diluted EPS, are summarized in the accompanying KPI table.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions.** Net sales rose 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million as demand for our liquid-cooling portfolio continued to build. The CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger, launched in the second quarter with two hyperscale customers, is now ramping, and the two hyperscale awards booked in Q3 extend our platform deeper into the largest data-center builds in the world. Segment backlog grew 22.0% year over year to $574.2 million. This backlog converts to revenue over the coming quarters and into fiscal 2027, giving us unusually strong visibility into the growth trajectory of the business.

**Building Controls & Valves.** Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% year over year, reflecting softer commercial construction activity and a temporary pause in new GV-400 orders from several OEM customers pending the recall notice. Segment backlog was stable, up 0.6% year over year.

On the recall itself: on September 22, we filed with the CPSC under the Fast Track program to voluntarily recall approximately 41,200 GV-400 and GV-410 series combination gas valves shipped to OEM customers in date codes 2507–2612. Root cause is fully identified — a single out-of-spec supplier lot of diaphragm compound associated with a supplier change made in the first quarter of 2025 — and corrective action is complete. Replacement valves have been shipping from our Mequon plant since September 28, and no injuries have been reported. We also notified Health Canada in parallel. In the third quarter we recorded a $21.6 million charge covering field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement, and logistics. We said we would put customers first in this program, and we have.

## Outlook

We are updating our full-year fiscal 2026 outlook to reflect current BCV conditions and the temporary GV-400 order pause: net sales of $1.66–1.70 billion (previously $1.78–1.84 billion) and adjusted EBITDA of $205–215 million (previously $255–270 million). The update is driven by core commercial HVAC softness and prudent assumptions about the pace at which paused GV-400 orders resume — not by anything we see in data-center demand, which continues to strengthen.

Project Keystone remains central to the recovery: $35 million of run-rate savings by the second quarter of fiscal 2027, delivered through product-line simplification, procurement actions, and structural cost reduction. With the recall charge non-recurring and data-center volumes contributing a growing share of revenue, we see a clear path to margin recovery as fiscal 2027 backlog converts.

We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. Our capital priorities are disciplined and straightforward: convert the record backlog into revenue and cash, complete the recall program for our customers, and fund the highest-return growth in TDC.

## Closing

This quarter tested our execution, and across the recall and the data-center ramp our teams delivered. To our 6,200 employees: thank you for the speed and care you brought to the recall program and to our hyperscale customers. To the OEM partners working alongside us on the GV-400 program: thank you for your partnership. The demand signal in our backlog is the strongest in our history, and we intend to convert it into results.

Dana Whitcombe
President & Chief Executive Officer

Mark Ostrander
EVP & Chief Financial Officer
